To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a third of exposed workers and half of exposed workers with physical health complaints attributed their complaints to the air crash, and that attribution was associated with the type of disaster work, the immediate disaster scene, the personal disaster experience, the presence of a close one affected, and the perception of the disaster as the most traumatic experience in life.
almost half of the exposed workers attributed their complaints to the disaster and this was associated with the types of disaster-related tasks they performed.
almost half of the workers with physical complaints attribute their complaints to the disaster and its aftermath.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attribution in post-disasters.
attribution of physical complaints to disaster, and is not concerned with the attribution of physical complaints in general.
attribution of physical complaints after the air disaster in the Bijlmermeer district of Amsterdam, The Netherlands, in 1992.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

attribution to the disaster is associated with physical complaints in the aftermath of the air disaster in 1992, and that attribution may be a risk factor for the development and persistence of long-term physical complaints in the disaster aftermath.
attribution is an important determinant of post-disaster health problems and should not be ignored.
the disaster and its aftermath were not associated with excess morbidity, and that attribution of physical complaints to it was not associated with excess complaints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the attribution of long-term physical complaints by exposed rescue workers to a past disaster is common, and is associated with the type and extent of disaster exposure.

the attribution of long-term physical complaints is not limited to a single disaster event, but is a general and long-term process that can be triggered by any event that has a strong impact on the affected individual.
the attribution of physical complaints to an air disaster is a complex process and that the attribution process is not the same for all workers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attribution is an important factor in post-disaster physical health problems and that it should be included in future disaster research and health care provision.
the health of exposed disaster workers should not be neglected, even if no excess morbidity is predicted.
the disaster-related health problems of rescue workers are not necessarily related to the disaster itself, but may be the result of attribution.
